newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine commmittee upholds land deal-official.
newsitem.headline: Philippine commmittee upholds land deal-official.

text.p: A presidential committee has upheld the multi-million peso land deal entered into by Centennial City and Ital-Thai Development Plc with state-owned Philippine Estate Authority, press secretary Hector Villanueva said on Friday.
"We are upholding the contract as a sound contract," Villanueva told reporters when asked about the report submitted by a three-man committee to President Fidel Ramos.
Villanueva said the deal "is in the long run favourable to the country."
"It is a joint venture (on) something that has still to be developed. This is not a real estate sale," he said.
Villanueva said he had not read the report, but the decision was relayed to him by committee chairman Salvador Enriquez. Enriquez was not available for comment.
President Ramos is yet to ratify the committee's report.
The deal involves the reclamation and the development of 750 hectares of land in Manila Bay.

Last year, Senate president Ernesto Maceda alleged the government entered into a disadvantageous deal since the property was grossly underpriced. He urged for the cancellation of the deal which was already approved by Ramos.
Other members of the consortium include Centennial's parent Guoco Holdings (Philippines) Inc.

Guoco Holdings president Micky Yong earlier defended the deal saying it was not underpriced. The valuation of 1,250 pesos per square metre was based on appraisals made by three independent appraisers, he said.
Both Centennial and Guoco shares had slumped when the controversy broke out late last year.
Centennial shares had fallen to as low as 1.88 pesos from 4.50 pesos in mid-November. It closed at 3.20 pesos on Friday.
Guoco Holdings slipped to a low of 4.20 pesos from more than 6.00 pesos by mid-November. It closed at 4.80 pesos on Friday.
